A Hall of Fame coach and longtime mentor of 23-time Olympic gold medalist Michael Phelps, Bob Bowman begins his third season as Director of Swimming and Diving and Head Men's Swimming Coach at The University of Texas in 2026-27. In his first two years in Austin, Bowman has guided the Longhorns to back-to-back NCAA Championships and SEC titles. He was hired at Texas in April 2024 after transforming the Arizona State program into a national champion over nine seasons.
Bowman became just the seventh head coach in the history of the Texas Men’s Swimming and Diving program, joining Tex Robertson (1935-43, 1946-50), Art Burnham (1944), Bob Bollinger (1945), Hank Chapman (1951-69), Pat Patterson (1970-78) and the legendary Eddie Reese (1979-2024). Reese, who completed his 46th season at Texas in 2023-24, guided the Longhorns to an NCAA-leading 15 national team championships, 13 NCAA runner-up finishes and 36 top-three finishes at the NCAA Championships. Reese continues to serve in a coach emeritus role for the Texas Swimming and Diving program.
During the 2025-26 season, Texas captured its second straight NCAA team title. This marked the program's NCAA-best 17th national championship and the third consecutive year that Bowman had led a team to the national title after guiding Arizona State to the 2024 crown. The Longhorns also won their second straight SEC Championship, extending the program's streak to 47 consecutive years with a conference title.
In his first season (2024-25) in Austin, Bowman guided Texas to the NCAA Championship while also claiming the SEC crown in its first year competing in the league.
Bowman has enjoyed one of the most decorated international coaching careers in the history of the sport. He is the longtime coach of Michael Phelps, the most decorated Olympian in history with 23 gold medals. Bowman served as the head men’s coach for Team USA at the 2016 Rio Olympic Games and previously worked as an assistant coach at the 2004 Athens, 2008 Beijing and 2012 London Olympic Games. Working alongside Reese, who served as Team USA’s head coach in 2004 and 2008, Bowman helped Phelps claim eight total medals, including six gold and two bronze, at the 2004 Olympic Games. Four years later at the 2008 Games, Phelps won eight Olympic gold medals, a feat never before accomplished in a single Olympiad.
A veteran collegiate head coach, Bowman arrived at Texas after spending nine seasons transforming Arizona State University into one of the top men’s swimming and diving programs in the country. He served as the head men’s and women’s swimming coach at ASU beginning in the 2015-16 season.
When Bowman took over in Tempe, the Sun Devil men were coming off a fifth-place showing at the Pac-12 Championship and did not score at the NCAA Championship meet in 2015. Arizona State had not finished in the top three at the Pac-12 meet since a second-place showing in 1995 and only had five top-three finishes at the conference meet since 1980. At the national level, ASU had never earned a team trophy (top four) at the NCAA Championship and had not finished higher than sixth place at the national meet when the Sun Devils accomplished that in 1982.
Bowman guided the Sun Devil men to the national title for the first time in program history at the 2024 NCAA Championship. Arizona State posted a dominant 79-point victory (523.5-444.5) over runner-up California at the national meet, winning seven individual or relay titles while setting three NCAA records and nine school records. A total of 14 Sun Devil athletes earned All-America honors during the four-day meet.
The Sun Devils also won their second-consecutive Pac-12 Championship in 2024 by a margin of 303 points, marking the second-highest margin of victory in conference history and the largest since California in 1995. ASU captured 16 individual and relay titles, broke 11 school records and set three NCAA records during its run to the Pac-12 Championship.

## Third Season at Texas
Erik Posegay begins his third year as Associate Head Coach for the Men's Swimming and Diving program at The University of Texas in 2026-27. In his first two years in Austin, Posegay has helped the Longhorns to back-to-back NCAA Championships and SEC titles.
During the 2025-26 season, Texas captured its second straight NCAA team title, marking the program's NCAA-best 17th national championship. The Longhorns also won their second straight SEC Championship, extending the program's streak to 47 consecutive years with a conference title.
In his first season (2024-25) in Austin, Posegay helped Texas win the NCAA Championship while also claiming the SEC crown in its first year competing in the league.
Posegay arrived on the Forty Acres after a two-year stint with USA Swimming, where he served as the National Junior Team Program Director beginning in April 2022 before being promoted to National Junior Team Director and National Coach in September 2023. As the program director, he led all aspects of the National Junior Team by developing and maintaining programs that served as the pathway from elite-level age-group swimmers towards the Olympic Games. Upon his promotion, he added coaching duties for national team camps at the Olympic Training Center as well as for national team athletes at Pro Swim Series events.
Posegay has coached numerous Olympians, U.S. National Team members, World Championships competitors and Paralympians during his coaching career. He served as the head coach for USA Swimming at the 2024 World Aquatics Championships, guiding the United States to Team of the Meet honors after the U.S. claimed the most gold medals (8) and total medals (20).
His international coaching experience includes time as an assistant for the United States at the 2015 Open Water World Championships, the 2013 Duel in the Pool and 2010 Junior Pan Pacific Championships. He led the U.S. squad to team titles at all three events. Posegay also served as the head coach for North Macedonia at the 2016 Rio Olympic Games and an assistant coach for France at the 2014 European Championships.
Prior to his time with USA Swimming, Posegay spent four seasons on the University of Wisconsin coaching staff as an assistant coach (2018-21) and associate head coach (2021-22). During his stint with the Badgers, he was tasked with leading the distance and individual medley groups and assisting with recruiting. From 2016-18, he was an assistant coach at Penn State University, working primarily with the distance, individual medley and stroke events.
Beginning in 2011, Posegay spent five years at the North Baltimore Aquatic Club (NBAC). He began his time at the NBAC as an assistant under Bowman before being promoted to head coach and CEO of the club in 2015, when Bowman departed to become the head coach at Arizona State.
Posegay served as the head coach at Parkland High School and Parkland Aquatic Club (Allentown, Pa.) for six years, guiding the Parkland girls' team to the Class 3A high school state championship in 2006. He began his coaching career as an assistant at Emmaus Aquatic Club and Emmaus High School (Emmaus, Pa.) from 2002-05.
A native of Allentown, Pa., Posegay graduated from Albright College (Reading, Pa.) in 2002 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science.
